page: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) running at 2.5 GHz on the arm64 architecture, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 937 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities in multi-core and single-core stress-ng tests, with scores of 6056.47 and 1520.08 respectively. However, memory and processing bottlenecks are evident in other areas. The passmark CPU score of 2687.46 and encryption score of 541.67 are rated poor, while the passmark database operations score of 2579.99 is weak. Memory bandwidth for large block reads (71.67 GB/sec) and writes (34.86 GB/sec) is average, but small block cached reads (236.01 GB/sec) and overall passmark memory score (1639.26) fall into the weak category. Text processing and LLM inference tasks also show poor performance, with prompt processing at 125.16 tokens/sec for a 135M model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i4g.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for storage-heavy workloads that do not require intensive CPU calculations. The dedicated ARM-based cores provide predictable execution but lack advanced vector or matrix extensions. This server is suited for localized database hosting, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications where local NVMe read/write speeds are prioritized over raw computational throughput or high-speed network bandwidth.
